Autonomous Interstellar Seed Factory. A proposed robotic expedition that could use locally available resources to build a limited industrial base, if sufficiently capable self-reliant machinery becomes feasible.

This database covers the technology as item 214 entry 31 of Manon's "100 Technologies Beyond Omega (A)" catalog, section "Interstellar Engineering". It is the public edition: every factual claim below is drawn from real public science and engineering, honestly labeled.

Feasibility tier: unresolved. The concept is studied (Freitas, 1980); the machinery does not exist.

Classification: public database. This record profiles the technology; companion records cover known science, constraints, approaches, tools, unresolved problems, evidence, and outlook.

title: Autonomous Interstellar Seed Factory - Known Science Foundations
description: Public edition: A proposed robotic expedition that could use locally available resources to build a limited industrial base, if sufficiently capable self-reliant machinery becomes feasible.
body:
Known science foundations of Autonomous Interstellar Seed Factory.

Freitas's 1980/1982 NASA study detailed a self-replicating lunar factory. Modern ISRU and robotics advance components. But a seed factory that lands at another star and builds industry from local resources is beyond every demonstrated capability — the 'if' in the description is doing heavy work.

Key quantity check (Freitas factory mass in tons / mass landed on the Moon to date in tons): computed ratio 0.2 against the reference value, relative error 0, within the stated tolerance of 0.4. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

title: Autonomous Interstellar Seed Factory - Physical and Engineering Constraints
description: Public edition: A proposed robotic expedition that could use locally available resources to build a limited industrial base, if sufficiently capable self-reliant machinery becomes feasible.
body:
Physical and engineering constraints on Autonomous Interstellar Seed Factory.

Interstellar travel itself is unsolved. Autonomous industry from raw resources is unproven even on the Moon. The concept assumes breakthroughs in propulsion, robotics, and AI.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 6.7 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is landed mass vs replication closure at 6.7 orders of magnitude (landed mass larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.

body:
Unresolved problems for Autonomous Interstellar Seed Factory, in priority order (research burden index 36, 3 blocking):

Propulsion to another star (severity 3/3, tractability 1/3, BLOCKING; priority 12).

Autonomous industrial bootstrap (severity 3/3, tractability 1/3, BLOCKING; priority 12).

A credible mission design (severity 3/3, tractability 1/3, BLOCKING; priority 12).

These are open problems, stated plainly. A technology with unresolved blocking problems is not ready, whatever its promise.
